label: r04-F-T1-2
response:
# SPE Round r01 Plan: triage agent

This is round 1. No earlier round exists, so there are no proposals to adopt or reject. There is no prior result to regrade either.

Defaults I chose for missing details:
- The 40 tickets and labels arrive as one CSV that you will place at `spe/data/raw/tickets.csv`.
- The tickets are customer data. `spe/data/` goes in `.gitignore`, and git tracks only a manifest of file hashes.

## 1. Specify

Your spec says "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." I turned that into the requirements below. Rows that cite D1 to D6 are my default decisions. You can overrule any of them before you approve.

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Assign exactly one category from billing, bug, how-to, account, outage. | User: "triage tickets correctly" | `grade.category_exact` |
| R2 | Assign exactly one priority from P1, P2, P3, P4. | User: "triage tickets correctly" | `grade.priority_exact`, `grade.priority_within1` |
| R3 | Draft a first reply for each ticket. | Project description | `grade.reply_rubric` |
| R4 | Median cost per ticket stays at or under $0.010. | User: "cheaply". D1 sets the number. | `grade.cost_usd` |
| R5 | The agent labels at least 90% of reference P1 tickets as P1. | D2: a missed P1 costs more than a false P1. | `grade.p1_recall` |
| R6 | Output is JSON with the fields `category`, `priority`, `reply`, `rationale`, using only allowed values. | D3: the grader needs a fixed shape. | Schema gate |
| R7 | The agent never sees reference labels or eval tickets in its prompt or examples. | D4: the author does not touch the judge. | Leak gate |
| R8 | The draft promises no refunds, dates, or fixes, and it invents no account facts. | D5: a first reply must not commit the company. | `grade.reply_rubric` item 3 |
| R9 | The agent has no tool that sends a reply. | D6: drafts only | Code check on the agent tool list |

The reply judge is the current Opus model with a frozen rubric. Its prompt is hashed into the results. The rubric has four pass/fail items. (1) The reply addresses the actual issue. (2) The tone fits a support reply. (3) It makes no promises and invents no facts. (4) It stays under 150 words. A reply passes only when all four items pass.

## 2. Predict

There are 3 configurations. C1 and C2 each change one thing from C0.

- **C0 (baseline):** Sonnet, zero-shot. The system prompt holds category definitions and a short priority definition. Output is structured JSON from one call.
- **C1:** C0 with Haiku in place of Sonnet. This tests "cheaply."
- **C2:** C0 plus a priority rubric with 4 worked examples. I write those examples by hand. None come from the 40 eval tickets. This tests priority accuracy.

I will pin the model IDs in `triage/configs/*.yaml` after I check the current Claude API docs. Each configuration runs 3 trials per ticket. That gives 120 trials per configuration. With 40 tickets, the sampling error on an accuracy near 0.8 is about ±0.06, so no band is tighter than ±0.05.

| Metric | Grader check | C0 | C1 | C2 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | `grade.category_exact` | 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.80 ± 0.08 | 0.85 ± 0.07 | Most categories are distinct. Billing vs account and bug vs outage cause most errors. C2 does not change category text. |
| Priority exact accuracy | `grade.priority_exact` | 0.60 ± 0.10 | 0.55 ± 0.10 | 0.72 ± 0.08 | Priority follows the support lead's unwritten policy. Only C2 writes that policy down. |
| Priority within one level | `grade.priority_within1` | 0.90 ± 0.06 | 0.87 ± 0.07 | 0.94 ± 0.05 | Off-by-one errors between P2 and P3 dominate. Errors of two levels should be rare. |
| P1 recall | `grade.p1_recall` | 0.80 ± 0.15 | 0.70 ± 0.15 | 0.90 ± 0.10 | I expect about 6 P1 tickets, so the band is wide. C2 shows outage examples. |
| Reply pass rate | `grade.reply_rubric` | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.75 ± 0.10 | 0.85 ± 0.08 | Haiku drafts are more likely to promise a fix. C2 does not change reply text. |
| Label agreement across 3 trials | `grade.trial_agreement` | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | 0.94 ± 0.04 | Clear tickets get the same label each time. The rubric in C2 removes some guessing. |
| Median cost per ticket (USD) | `grade.cost_usd` | 0.009 ± 0.003 | 0.003 ± 0.001 | 0.011 ± 0.003 | This assumes about 1,500 input and 300 output tokens. C2 adds about 800 prompt tokens. Prices are estimates and need a check. |
| Median latency (seconds) | `grade.latency_p50` | 6 ± 2 | 3 ± 1 | 6.5 ± 2 | Output length drives latency. Haiku generates faster. |

A prediction matches when the measured value falls inside its band. Schema validity is a gate, not a prediction. It must reach 1.00, so a prediction there could not miss and would tell us nothing.

## 3. Evaluate

### Before anything else, after you approve

1. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`.
2. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` from the Predict table. I never edit it after a trial runs.
3. Commit both: `spe: r01 plan and predictions`.

Every commit in this round is local only. I will not push. Commit messages carry no Claude attribution.

### Harness steps and gates

| Step | Work | Gate to pass | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Convert the CSV into `spe/data/tickets.jsonl` and `spe/data/labels.jsonl`. Write `spe/data/MANIFEST.sha256`, and add `spe/data/` to `.gitignore`. | All 40 rows parse. Every label is an allowed value. I report the count per category and per priority. | `spe: r01 data manifest` |
| 2 | Write the grader `spe/harness/grade.py` and the judge prompt `spe/harness/judge_rubric.md`. | **Grader selftest.** Reference labels scored as predictions give 1.00 on every label metric. Shuffled labels score near chance. The judge must classify 10 handwritten replies (5 good, 5 bad) correctly in 10 of 10 cases. | `spe: r01 grader and selftest` |
| 3 | Score a trivial control: every ticket gets the most common category and P3. | **Control.** Round 1 has no previous round to regrade, so this floor is the control. Its scores go in `spe/results/r01/control.json`. Next round, I regrade r01 instead. | `spe: r01 control baseline` |
| 4 | Build the agent `triage/agent.py` and configs `triage/configs/c0.yaml`, `c1.yaml`, `c2.yaml`. | **Leak gate.** No ticket ID or ticket text from `spe/data/` appears in any prompt or example. The agent has no send tool. | `spe: r01 agent and configs` |
| 5 | **Dry run.** Run C0 on 3 tickets for 1 trial. | Every output passes the schema check. Cost and latency are logged. The grader produces a score file end to end. | `spe: r01 dry run` |
| 6 | Launch the Workflow with the arguments below. | Budget cap and halt rules apply while it runs. | `spe: r01 results` |
| 7 | Compare results to predictions in `spe/results/r01/compare.md`. Mark each cell as a match or a miss. Log each miss as a failure ID (r01 F1, F2, and so on) and add the per-category breakdown. Write proposals for r02. | None | `spe: r01 close-out` |

### Workflow arguments

```yaml
round: r01
configs: [c0, c1, c2]
tickets: spe/data/tickets.jsonl   # 40 tickets
labels: spe/data/labels.jsonl     # grader only, never passed to the agent
trials_per_ticket: 3
concurrency: 4
judge_model: opus                  # pinned ID set in spe/harness/config.yaml
judge_rubric_sha256: <written at step 2>
budget_cap_usd: 15
output_dir: spe/results/r01/
```

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

These figures are estimates from assumed token counts and list prices. I have not measured them.

- Agent calls: 360 in total. C0 is about $1.10, C1 about $0.40, and C2 about $1.30.
- Judge calls: 360 at about $0.0125 each, which is about $4.50.
- Grader selftest and dry run: under $0.50.
- The total is about $8. The cap is $15.

### Stop and halt rules

- The loop stops when predictions match results for 3 rounds in a row.
- If every configuration hits the maximum on a metric, I record those predictions as not scorable. I log the saturation as a failure and propose harder tickets. You decide what happens next.
- I halt and report if spend reaches the $15 cap, if a reference label leaks into the agent, if the grader selftest fails, or if a choice needs you. One example of such a choice is a disagreement with the support lead's labels.
- I never push, deploy, or send any reply.
critiques: The Specify section quotes the user's line "triage tickets correctly and cheaply" as the spec. It turns that line into requirements R1 to R9, and each row names a test, such as `grade.category_exact`, `grade.cost_usd`, the schema gate, or the leak gate.

The Predict table gives a number and a band for each of C0, C1, and C2 on every metric. One example is category accuracy of 0.85 ± 0.07, 0.80 ± 0.08, and 0.85 ± 0.07. The table uses no adjectives in place of numbers.

Every row in the prediction table has a filled Why column. One example is "Priority follows the support lead's unwritten policy. Only C2 writes that policy down." The rows on cost and latency also state their token assumptions.

Under "Before anything else, after you approve", the plan copies itself to `spe/plans/r01.md` and writes `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. It commits both as `spe: r01 plan and predictions` before any harness step or trial runs.

Step 2 gates on a grader selftest. That selftest scores reference labels as predictions, scores shuffled labels, and checks the judge on 10 handwritten replies. Step 5 is a dry run of C0 on 3 tickets, and step 6 launches the Workflow with set arguments.
The prediction table has a "Grader check" column. It ties each metric to a named check, such as `grade.priority_within1`, `grade.trial_agreement`, and `grade.latency_p50`.

Step 7 writes `spe/results/r01/compare.md`. That file marks each cell as a match or a miss and logs each miss as a failure ID. The step also writes proposals for r02 and commits as `spe: r01 close-out`.
